If a new figure is created by attaching a border of white tiles with the same size and shape as the others, what will be the difference between the total number of white tiles and the total number of black tiles in the new figure?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a complete large hexagonal cluster composed of regular hexagonal tiles of the same size. Looking by horizontal rows, the row lengths are 3, 4, 5, 4, 3, for a total of 19 pieces. The outer-ring tiles are all black, and inside there are 6 white tiles surrounding the 1 black tile in the middle; this is consistent with the 13 black tiles and 6 white tiles given in the problem statement. Then reason: The original figure is a hexagonal tile cluster with side length 3. When adding one ring of white tiles of the same size outside it, the number of newly added tiles is 6 × 3 = 18. The newly added 18 pieces are all white, so in the new figure the total number of white tiles is 6 + 18 = 24, and the number of black tiles remains 13. The difference between the two is 24 − 13 = 11.

Use the hexagonal-tile ring rule: adding a one-tile-thick border around a hexagonal cluster of side length 3 adds 6 × 3 = 18 new tiles.
